html:
The Waanyi are an Aboriginal Australian people of the country south of the Gulf of Carpentaria, across the border of Queensland and the Northern Territory.

Their country takes in Lawn Hill Gorge, now Boodjamulla National Park, and the fossil beds of Riversleigh, famous for the remains of ancient mammals. The Waanyi language belongs to the small Garrwan family with that of the Garrwa. Other neighbours were the Ganggalida on the coast and the Gunindiri to the west.

Cattle stations came in the 1880s with violent clashes. The novelist Alexis Wright is a Waanyi woman, and her novel Carpentaria is set in this Gulf country.
sum: The Waanyi are an Aboriginal Australian people of the country south of the Gulf of Carpentaria, across the border of Queensland and the Northern Territory.
